items.title: Design optional Intune cleanup after successful archive and Entra deletion
items.problem: Post-v1 proposes Intune removal; Graph success and archival are strict prerequisites.
acceptance: Removal plan identifies exact owned Intune object and archive receipt.
Absent archive, failed Entra deletion or ambiguous match prevents action; implementation and live deletion are separate tasks.
validation: Use the offline commands in the registered validation workflow; record the exact commands, revision and results before implementation is complete.
evidence: At source baseline 08f5efa647f94d1414447973b6ee036a130c68b1, docs/intune-removal-plan.md defines an inert closed plan contract that keeps tenantId, Entra object id, Entra deviceId, Intune managedDevice id, exact archive/index versions and cleanupRunId distinct and bound. It requires unique non-collapsing pre-archive discovery, exact-version archive readback, Entra DELETE acknowledgement plus direct absence observation, and post-Entra direct Intune target revalidation; labels, users, same-tenant relationships and newest-heartbeat selection cannot establish ownership or authorization.

The refusal matrix blocks absent, incomplete, ambiguous, foreign, unknown, stale or conflicting evidence. Existing archivedDeletedDevices rows and archive-index v1.0 cannot mint a trustworthy plan after the fact because the summary drops SecretVersion and IndexSecretName while the index has no tenantId and permits a null Intune id. A future dedicated collector must create contemporaneous tenant-bound evidence; implementation, permission grant and live deletion remain separate authorized tasks.

Microsoft Graph v1.0 documentation reviewed 2026-10-13 identifies DELETE /deviceManagement/managedDevices/{managedDeviceId} with DeviceManagementManagedDevices.ReadWrite.All and active Intune tenant licensing. The design excludes the separate retire/wipe device actions. PowerShell 7.6.6 parser, JSON, canonical permission and backlog schemas, generated backlog, Markdown links, contract-example binding, git diff check and Pester 5.7.1 passed, 86/86. Pinned Bicep 0.46.1 compiled successfully and differed from tracked compiler 0.42.1 output only in nested _generator version/hash metadata. No tenant/auth/archive/provider call, deletion, permission grant, schedule, infrastructure or default change ran.

Independent review passed both original discovery/design criteria on 2026-10-13, including exact source mappings, unchanged current permission requirements, synthetic contract consistency and fresh primary Microsoft API documentation. This closes the design item only; no schema/generator/executor, deletion authorization, live absence or endpoint outcome is implemented or proven.

items.title: Design optional Defender cleanup after successful archive and Entra deletion
items.problem: Post-v1 proposes MDE removal with separate consent and API boundaries.
acceptance: Document supported exact-device API and least permission requirements from current primary sources.
No inferred hostname match or implied destructive authorization; unsupported API is recorded as a gap.
validation: Use the offline commands in the registered validation workflow; record the exact commands, revision and results before implementation is complete.
evidence: At source baseline 2e5386f4da4537ee951037d11db41b3896c4f64b, current Microsoft primary documentation reviewed 2026-10-13 showed no supported machine-record deletion route in the published Defender for Endpoint API catalog. docs/defender-cleanup-design.md records this bounded unsupported gap without claiming universal absence. It documents the exact-ID offboard POST and its Machine.Offboard permission only as a separate endpoint lifecycle operation that is not chosen as an automatic deletion fallback.

The design distinguishes tenantId, Entra object id, Entra deviceId, Defender machine id, cleanupRunId and exact archive/index versions. It refuses hostname and latest-heartbeat inference, duplicate aadDeviceId rows, nullable or hunting-only machine IDs, mixed or stale evidence and absent exact-target authorization. Existing source collapses duplicate Defender inventory/hunting rows, archive-index v1.0 has no tenant binding, and the job summary loses archive/index versions, so existing records cannot mint a trustworthy action plan after the fact.

Published route requirements are recorded without granting or claiming effective permission: Machine.Read.All for inventory, Machine.Offboard for the separate offboard action, and the broad Machine.ReadWrite.All currently documented for exact-machine and machine-action reads as a least-privilege qualification gap. PowerShell 7.6.6 parser, JSON, canonical permission/backlog schemas, generated backlog, Markdown links, original-criteria preservation, protected-path comparison, git diff check and Pester 5.7.1 passed 86/86. Pinned Bicep 0.46.1 compiled successfully and differed from tracked output only in nested _generator version/hash metadata. No auth, provider, archive, tenant, endpoint action, permission grant, schedule, infrastructure, runtime, schema or default change ran.

Independent review passed both original discovery criteria on 2026-10-13: fresh primary API/permission documentation, the explicitly bounded unsupported deletion gap, real-source identity/provenance limitations, and no implied destructive authorization. This closes the design assessment only; offboarding is not selected, no executor or permission is added, and no service or endpoint result is proven.

items.title: Add optional NotOnboarded and Unmanaged dynamic-group proposals
items.problem: The existing stale groups do not express these additional cohorts.
scope: tests/ (actual local proposal/classifier and disabled-boundary fixtures)
acceptance: Preview membership and valid rule syntax from fixtures before any group creation.
Disabled options require no extra Graph permissions and are explicitly excluded from default disabling.
validation: Use the offline commands in the registered validation workflow; record the exact commands, revision and results before implementation is complete.
evidence: At source baseline 0c5290ee1f91bf796d6c01b07ad638995a2d072e, scripts/New-DeviceDynamicGroupProposal.ps1 adds a default-disabled local-only proposal CLI. It produces deterministic prospective and existing-attribute previews from bounded provided fixtures, round-trips only the two canonical extensionAttribute equality rules, reports an empty permission set, publisherPresent=false and groupCreationReady=false, and contains no provider, attribute, group or lifecycle action path.

Unmanaged inclusion requires a complete fresh Intune fixture with no exact managedDevice.azureADDeviceId match. NotOnboarded inclusion requires exactly one fresh valid Defender machine record with an exact aadDeviceId match and onboardingStatus CanBeOnboarded. Tenant/hash/freshness mismatch, unavailable/NoData/incomplete collection, absent or ambiguous Defender matches, malformed or duplicate identity, unsupported state, and unowned or stale current attributes remain Unknown. The fixture declarations establish only provided-fixture consistency, not authenticated capture, ownership, authorization or published state.

PowerShell 7.6.6 parsed 16 files with zero errors. Pester 5.7.1 passed 109/109 with zero failed, skipped or not-run tests. Eight JSON files parsed; canonical backlog and permission schemas, both proposal fixture schemas, backlog semantics and generated Markdown, original criteria and unrelated-record preservation, relative Markdown links, protected runtime/workflow/infrastructure byte comparison, and tracked/new-file whitespace checks passed. Bicep was not recompiled because infra/main.bicep and its tracked JSON and parameters match the verified baseline bytes; hosted validation will compile the unchanged source. No authentication, provider, tenant, archive, endpoint, permission, attribute, group, lifecycle, schedule or infrastructure action ran.

Independent review correction validates raw JSON collection and scalar types before classification: object-shaped devices or records, array-shaped GUIDs, malformed attribute objects, and non-integer attribute slots remain bounded Unknown instead of being coerced into positive evidence. Prospective and existing-attribute previews remain independent, valid empty Intune records remain a complete no-match inventory, and kind values are normalized before rule round-trip checks. Focused Pester 5.7.1 passed 32/32 with zero failed, skipped or not-run tests on PowerShell 7.6.6. The earlier full 109/109 result is inherited and was not rerun for this narrow correction; hosted validation will run the full suite.

The consolidated scalar-contract correction preserves JSON arrays only for declared devices and records collections. Every declared provider-fixture scalar is type-checked before comparison or parsing; singleton arrays for Defender machine id, onboardingStatus, source type, collection state, fixture schemaVersion or fixture kind cannot qualify membership. ConvertFrom-Json -NoEnumerate plus an explicit top-level object check also rejects a singleton top-level JSON array. Actual helper and file-CLI regressions passed in focused Pester 5.7.1: 39/39 with zero failed, skipped or not-run tests on PowerShell 7.6.6. Other suites were unchanged and not rerun; the earlier full 109/109 result remains inherited and hosted validation remains pending.

Independent actual-helper and file-CLI review passed the complete scalar/collection boundary on PowerShell 7.6.6, preserving valid empty arrays and prospective/current-attribute independence. Both original local-only criteria are implemented. Focused Pester 5.7.1 passed 39/39 with no failures or skips; prior 109-test full-suite evidence is inherited for unchanged areas, not a full corrected-source rerun. Fresh hosted full validation and compilation are publication gates before merge. This completion records only offline provided-fixture proposals: authenticated capture, ownership, attribute publishing, Entra service-side rule validation, group creation, effective permissions and lifecycle integration remain separate unimplemented or unproven work.

evidence: 2026-10-07 source implementation from base c7b3e6eaa2a76722fc45c61b95084c41f93bab24: each successful new recovery archive receives a separate closed, bounded, version-bound metadata index before Entra deletion. Default discovery remains metadata-only; explicit UPN lookup reads bounded index values, and explicit recovery validates the exact indexed archive version. Legacy latest aliases remain visible when a newer archive has no index. Optional relationship-based primary-user collection defaults false and never changes eligibility or heartbeat selection.

Validation: PowerShell 7.6.6 / Pester 5.7.1 full suite 81/81 passed with zero failed, skipped or not-run; reader and permission suites on PowerShell 7.2.24 passed 44/44. Root independently replayed the full suite and parser, JSON, canonical permission schema and evidence hashes, Bicep, backlog rendering and diff checks. Independent exact 23-file review passed with a separate 49/49 focused replay; all ten earlier review findings were repaired. Failed r1 source and evidence were preserved.

Qualification remains source/offline only. The selected lab managedDevices read returned HTTP 403 before the direct users relationship was reached; cause remains unknown and no new permission was granted. No deployment, device action, real recovery read or human recovery drill was performed. Production deployment, effective grants, live relationship reads and recovery acceptance remain separate qualification work.

2026-10-10 synthetic Key Vault lab contract failed when all four discovery/recovery lookups returned no match; its terminal receipt reports completed role, vault, tombstone and resource-group cleanup. A separate synthetic loopback HTTP proof on PowerShell 7.6.6 confirmed native Invoke-RestMethod converts ISO timestamp tags to DateTime, causing both strict legacy and index validators to refuse valid metadata. The reader now parses raw HTTP JSON with DateKind String and preserves timestamp-shaped recovery strings; 86/86 offline tests passed. This repairs the confirmed source defect but does not establish live service acceptance or a human recovery drill.

items.problem: Larger hunting payloads need a bounded archive policy.
acceptance: Document the existing 24,000-byte compact UTF-8 payload ceiling, unchanged complete-payload refusal without chunking, and retention/recovery tradeoffs.

Keep existing Key Vault soft-delete retention and purge protection unchanged; distinguish deleted-secret recovery windows from active-archive expiration.
